fields.name: combination

fields.name: revision
fields.meaning: exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters; the provider audit, the plan and every evidence entry must carry the identical string

fields.name: profileId
fields.meaning: a non-empty string at behavior level (else profile-missing), handed to both inspectors as the expected profile; at the other levels it is only echoed

fields.name: scope
fields.meaning: field of an evidence entry: its providerId and combinationId must equal the request, else the entry is not valid evidence

fields.name: acceptedEvidence
fields.meaning: derived, not passed through: for each required kind the first matching entry (revision, status success, provider id, combination id) is reduced to kind, revision, source, runId and artifactRef

fields.name: byte_sha256
fields.meaning: field of an artifact reference: sha256 of the exact bytes, 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; compared with the hash of the bytes passed in (artifact-bytes-mismatch)

fields.name: size_bytes
fields.meaning: field of an artifact reference: the byte length of the artifact, a non-negative safe integer; compared with the length of the bytes passed in

fields.name: combinationId
fields.meaning: the id of a catalog entry as a hand-off names it; the expectation takes expected.combinationId, else expected.id

fields.name: provenance
fields.meaning: record handed in next to the persistence hand-off: status accepted, producerRevision of 40 hexadecimal characters, candidateRevision equal to the expected revision, combinationId, profileId, executionRef and an artifactRef equal to the reference of the hand-off field by field

fields.name: runtime_binding_hash

rules.statement: The layer is shadow only: applyAllowed is false in every plan shape and in every certification result, blocked or certified.

Each of the six modules imports only sibling modules of the layer and node:crypto; none of them has a computed import, a require call or a createRequire call, and none reads a clock, a random source or the process, prints or is asynchronous.

A combination is approved only when provider id, persistence id and key type together equal one of the three catalog entries; a changed, empty or missing part gives null, and parts taken from two entries are not approved.
The catalog hands out copies: changing an entry that listApprovedCombinations or resolveApprovedCombination returned changes nothing, and APPROVED_COMBINATIONS itself is frozen.

previewGeneration calls the emit function of the provider once, with force false, an empty reason, dryRun true and computeDiff false; for a combination outside the catalog and for a failed resource check it does not call emit at all.

The levels preview-tested and build-tested can end certified, but behavior-tested always ends blocked with behavior-handoff-not-integrated and certifiedLevel null, even when both hand-off inspections say eligible.

A revision is exactly 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters: a branch name, an upper-case sha, a shorter or longer string, an empty string, null or a missing value gives invalid-revision, and an evidence entry of another revision gives invalid-evidence.

At preview and build level the certification reads plain evidence entries (kind, revision, status success and a scope with provider id and combination id) and copies what an entry names as its artifact without checking it; it does not call validateBoundCertificationEvidence, which refuses the same entries.
The persistence hand-off passes only with a provenance status accepted; bound, pending, null and a missing status all give handoff-not-approved.

For JSON data, which is arrays and plain objects (objects whose prototype is Object.prototype) that hold strings, finite numbers, booleans, null and more arrays and plain objects, the hash of t16HashJson is the sha256 of the value written with two-space indentation and one final newline and with the keys of every object, at every depth, sorted by UTF-16 code unit, except that keys that are array indexes (the text of a whole number from 0 to 4294967294 without a leading zero, such as 2 and 10) come first, in numeric order; the runtime inspector reports that hash of the binding document as bindingHash.

t16HashJson does not hash every value. A BigInt (as the value, as an array element or as an enumerable string-keyed property, also when nested in other values) throws a TypeError. A cycle through plain objects and arrays, or a nesting deep enough to exhaust the stack, throws a RangeError, and a cycle through a class instance or an object without prototype throws a TypeError. Undefined, a function, a symbol and a call without an argument throw nothing and share one hash, that of the text undefined with a final newline; NaN, Infinity and null share one hash as well. A class instance and an object without prototype are not sorted: their keys, and the keys of everything inside them, come out in the order in which the engine lists them (array indexes first, in numeric order, then the other keys in the order in which they were added), so the same keys added in another order can give another hash. Whenever it returns, the result is a string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
An artifact reference has exactly six fields and is compared field by field: a changed field, a changed size or a seventh field blocks the hand-off.

The runtime inspector compares the values of the binding, the pair, the evidence documents and the projection with each other and checks the format of candidate_hash only: an empty run id, an empty attempt nonce or a null contract hash stays eligible when every document repeats it, and a pair hash that is empty, null or 0 skips the comparison with the evidence document.
The status words are blocked, ready, certified and eligible and nothing else: no function of the layer answers unknown or partial.

For python-fastapi and typescript-express, authorization and patch of a generated resource are fail-closed stubs with one manual completion per resource and area, and recover is gated by the access stub; java-spring follows its provider policy and lists no manual completion.

Observed defect, not fixed: provider ids are looked up in plain objects, so the inherited names constructor, toString and hasOwnProperty pass; describeResourceGeneration then returns a generated decision whose fetch, authorization, patch and recover are undefined, and requiredEvidenceFor lists a function where an evidence kind belongs.
